engagement_title: Cedar Commons Farmers Market signage season: recover the market mark off a volunteer's apron, build the entrance banner and directional set at the sizes the site takes, and run a numbered plate for every stall off this season's roster
vertical: Community and civic events, a volunteer run weekend farmers market in a municipal park, Burlington, Vermont, May through October
real_brief_anchor: The ledger carries no quoted post for this line, so the anchor is stated as the commission shape rather than as a quotation, which is said plainly here rather than fabricated into a fake quote. The shape is the recurring community signage brief posted on Upwork and Freelancer.com by volunteer run markets, town fairs, church fetes and school fairs: a tiny or zero budget, an existing mark that survives only on merchandise or an old printed piece with no source file anywhere, a request for a banner and some directional signs the committee can take to a local sign shop, a per stall or per table numbered item at volume, and a plain sheet the committee can hand the printer. Two things those posts always share, and this task is built on both. The artwork must be RECOVERED rather than redrawn, because a nine year old volunteer drawn mark is the market's identity and the committee will notice a redraw instantly. And the deliverable is judged by whether a local sign shop can print it on coroplast and vinyl, not by how it looks on a screen. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what turns that into a full commission rather than a thin one: absolute units resolve to exact physical dimensions on the HTML to Express surface, an ink level trace off a photographed screen print recovers a real mark, and the sign shop's own plate card PDF converts into a live merge for a forty four stall run. Verdict STRENGTHEN honoured: the concept and the six item collateral set are kept intact and the depth is raised from what sat on one vector surface to five honestly counted ones.
client_one_liner: Our weekend market has outgrown its chalkboards, and the only artwork we still have of our own mark is a photograph of a volunteer's apron.
client_brief:
Cedar Commons Farmers Market, signage set

We are a volunteer run weekend market in a park in Burlington, Vermont. Thirty six to forty four stalls, May through October, free to the public. Vendors pay twenty five to sixty dollars a day and that is the entire budget, so all of this goes to a local sign shop on coroplast and vinyl. Nothing here goes to a fancy printer.

Right now we run on chalkboards and a bedsheet banner and it shows. People park in the wrong lot. They walk straight past the entrance. Vendors get asked where stall nineteen is forty times a morning.

What we have. Our mark was drawn by a volunteer's cousin nine years ago and screen printed onto aprons and tote bags. Nobody kept a file and the cousin is not reachable. The best surviving copy is a photograph of one of the aprons. We also have phone photographs of the site that our chair took one morning in May, and the sign shop's plate card artwork from two seasons ago, which they say they can reprint from as is.

What we need. A proper entrance banner at the size our fence takes. A set of yard signs that get people to the right parking lot, to the vendor rows and to the info tent, readable from a car. A numbered plate for every stall with the vendor's name on it, printed off our current roster, one per stall. A sheet the committee can hand the sign shop saying what goes where, how many and at what size. And a picture of a staked sign standing on our actual site, because half the committee cannot read a plan.

Cheerful, legible from a distance, few colours, and it lives outdoors in the rain. Not precious. And please tell us what our mark can and cannot do, because we would rather know now than after we have paid for forty four plates.
price_band_and_audience: A free public community market funded entirely by 25 to 60 dollar daily stall fees, audience the neighbourhood families and weekend walkers who come on foot or park in the wrong lot. The band is load bearing and it points the opposite way from a retail brief. At this budget the whole set has to be a small number of flat inks on white coroplast and vinyl, with type heavy enough to be read from a moving car and a mark reduced to a cut that survives at six inches and at eight feet. A refined luxury palette of soft tints and hairline rules is not merely off brief, it is unreadable outdoors and unprintable at this price, and it makes a free community market look like it is charging. Push the other way into carnival clip art and clashing brights and it undercuts a market whose vendors sell 9 dollar cheese and 30 dollar cut flowers, and the committee, who are volunteers with taste, will reject it. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 400 to 1,200 dollars fixed, often part donated.

brand_identity.sector: A volunteer-run weekend farmers market in a municipal park, free to the public, funded by daily stall fees.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, in a park in Burlington, Vermont. Volunteer-run, 36 to 44 stalls, open weekends May through October.
brand_identity.about: Cedar Commons is a neighbourhood farmers market that runs on weekends in a Burlington park, free to walk into and funded entirely by the vendors who pay a daily stall fee. It has outgrown its chalkboards and its bedsheet banner. The signage exists to get families to the right lot, past the entrance and to the stall they are looking for, printed cheaply and well at a local sign shop.
brand_identity.audience: Neighbourhood families and weekend walkers who arrive on foot or park in the wrong lot, plus the vendors and volunteers who run the morning. Read from a moving car and from across a field.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A free public market funded by 25 to 60 dollar daily stall fees, often part-donated. Everything prints on coroplast and vinyl at a local sign shop. Flat inks and heavy type, never a refined tint palette that would be unreadable outdoors and would make a free market look like it is charging.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a friendly high-contrast slab or bold grotesque, weighted to be read from a car. Wayfinding and schedule copy in a plain heavy sans with one clear instruction per sign. Real weight matters more than refinement.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, plain and welcoming, like a volunteer at the gate. Example line: "Cheerful, legible from a distance, few colours, and it lives outdoors in the rain. Not precious. Tell us what our mark can and cannot do."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The market mark was drawn nine years ago by a volunteer's cousin, who is not reachable, and screen-printed onto aprons and tote bags. No file of any kind was ever kept. The best surviving copy is a photograph of one apron folded on a picnic table. There is no vector art, so the mark has to be recovered from that photograph rather than redrawn.
brand_identity.values: Community and thrift. Recover the real mark rather than replace it, keep the set to a few flat inks that print cheaply, and tell the committee what the mark can and cannot do before they pay for plates.

assets_supplied.name: cedar_commons_apron.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of a volunteer's canvas apron with the market mark screen printed on it, folded on a picnic table in daylight.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The best copy of our mark that still exists anywhere."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark is a compound lockup, a cedar bough over an arched wordmark inside a ring rule, so a single compound selection returns the ring and the arch while silently dropping the bough, and a background removal on the ring hands back a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. The apron is coarse canvas, so the printed ink is broken at stroke level, and the fold runs through the lower third of the ring.

assets_supplied.name: cedar_commons_site/ (4 frames, phone camera)
assets_supplied.kind: Phone photographs of the market site taken one May morning: the park entrance and its fence, the gravel parking approach, the vendor row, and the info tent corner.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our chair took these one morning in May so you can see where things go."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The parking approach frame was shot into the light with the sky fully clipped behind the exact fence line where the sign has to stand, so a highlight recovery on that region returns success with nothing moved. Two of the four are off level, and the vendor row frame, the only one that includes the fence, has a delivery van parked across the position the mockup wants.

assets_supplied.name: cedar_commons_sign_blank.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of a blank white coroplast yard sign on its wire stake, pushed into the gravel by the parking approach, shot for scale.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "A blank sign on a stake so you can see how big they actually are."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The sign's lower edge and its wire stake sit at almost the same value as the wet gravel behind them, so a one call knockout returns a cutout that reads clean and complete at preview scale and is bitten along the stake and the bottom rail at full size. The blank also leans a few degrees in the gravel.

assets_supplied.name: cedar_commons_plate_card.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The sign shop's six by six inch stall plate artwork from two seasons ago, supplied as the press PDF they reprint from: a stall number block and a vendor name line.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The plate card the sign shop already has and says they can reuse."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The vendor name sits in a fixed measure frame that does not spill: a name longer than the frame simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so a long vendor name is truncated at trim while the merge reports success and the page count still matches the roster exactly. The card carries no bleed and none can be introduced into a template derived from a PDF.

assets_supplied.name: cedar_commons_stalls.csv
assets_supplied.kind: This season's roster as the stall committee keeps it: stall number, vendor name, category, zone.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The roster as it stands today. It changes most weeks but this is what we are printing from."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two rows carry the same stall number, and the zone column spells one zone two different ways, so a plate run taken straight off the file produces a duplicate and a zone that appears twice in the schedule. Neither is flagged anywhere in the file.

assets_supplied.name: cedar_commons_signage_list.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The committee's own list of what they think they need, with sizes written in feet and inches and quantities in the margin.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What we think we need. Correct us if we have got it wrong."

acceptance_bar: The mark is recovered rather than redrawn, complete with its bough, its arched wordmark and its ring rule, and a volunteer who has worn the apron for nine years recognises it.

The recovered mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and no filled disc where the ring's interior should be open.
There is a cut of the mark that survives at six inches on a stall plate and a cut that survives on a banner read from across a car park, and each is the one actually used in that place.

The entrance banner canvas is at the true proportion of the fence run the committee gave, its absolute units resolve to the stated scale, and the scale factor is named on the sheet the sign shop receives.
The directional signs are legible as a driver reads them: a few flat inks, one clear instruction each, and type sized for distance rather than for a screen.

The stall plate run has one plate per real stall, produced off the reconciled roster rather than off the raw file, and every vendor name on every plate is complete at trim. A truncated name fails even though the page count is right.
The roster is reconciled before anything is printed: the duplicate stall number and the double spelled zone are resolved and the resolution is stated.
The site photographs are levelled and brought to one morning look, and the mockup stands on a frame that can actually carry it rather than on the one that happened to include the fence.
No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no returned tradeoff record carries an upscale entry.
The staked sign in the mockup is cut cleanly all the way down its stake and along its bottom rail, judged at full size on the site photograph rather than at preview scale.

The banner, the yard signs, the schedule sheet and the mockup board arrive as one working file the committee can edit itself, each canvas keeping its own size, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.
The printer note states substrate, quantity, finished size, ink count and safe margin for every item, plus what the mark cannot do and what the process could not be given.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_adjust_highlights, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: All the recovery and all the photographic repair. It levels the phone frames, brings four site photographs shot in one uneven morning to one look, attempts the highlight work the parking approach frame needs, pulls the mark at ink level off a coarse canvas apron by naming the print's own visual properties per element rather than the garment it sits on, sets polarity, traces, performs the vector hygiene the tracer does not, builds the small size and large size cuts of the mark, and knocks the staked blank off the gravel for the mockup plate.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The entrance banner, the three directional yard signs, the signage schedule sheet and the staked mockup board as one native editable document carrying roots at several canvas sizes, which is the only surface in the connector that composes free form fixed canvas layout at true physical dimensions. Absolute units resolve exactly, so the banner and the yard signs can be authored at the proportions the site takes at a declared scale, every photograph must be inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, and the mark goes in as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper so it stays vector and stays on the artboard.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign document conversion, merge template authoring and render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (both as readout and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The stall plate run. The sign shop's own plate card PDF is reverse engineered into a live merge template bound to the reconciled roster and merged one record per page, which is the only route in the connector to a genuine per record run at forty four plates. Merged to InDesign first and rendered separately, because the merge tool silently ignores resolution and only the render step yields real print resolution proofs the committee can read.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The signage type system across the banner, the yard signs and the schedule sheet. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on cheerful and distance legible rather than precious or corporate. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, which matters more here than usual because the whole set depends on real weight at distance, every name must be laundered into canonical form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the type falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources one camera scale outdoor frame the market does not have, for the schedule sheet's cover and as the fallback ground the mockup can stand on, IP clean and with generative tech candidates excluded. The Boards half persists the shortlist the volunteer committee, who are distributed and meet once a month, actually sign off from, placed within the twelve per call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The banner, the yard signs, the schedule and the mockup need an authored fixed canvas document at true physical proportions, the forty four plates need a genuine record per page run against the sign shop's own template, and the mark is recovery work. Nothing else in the connector composes free form layout and nothing else does per record volume.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role so that thirty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which site frame and which is the plate card.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview the apron, the four site frames and the sign blank and triage them: what the mark is actually built from, which frames are off level, which frame includes the fence, where the sign has to stand, and how the blank's stake sits against the gravel.
trajectory.judgement: The photographs are the only thing that can settle what the mark is made of and which frame can carry a mockup at all. The committee's list says what they want, not what the pictures can do.
trajectory.produces: A per asset triage note covering mark structure, frame level, sign position and subject against ground contrast.

trajectory.action: Straighten the off level site frames and the leaning blank, before any crop or bounds decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and a mockup built on a tilted horizon reads as a mistake to a committee.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Bring the four site frames to one May morning look, correcting each toward one target with its own call, and work the sky and the fence line on the parking approach frame where the sign has to stand.
trajectory.judgement: One batched call applies one identical parameter set to four frames shot at different angles into different light, which is exactly wrong. The target is a set of pictures of one place on one morning.
trajectory.produces: Four corrected site masters with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark: an ink level selection naming the print's own visual properties rather than the apron, taken element by element because the lockup is compound, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own returned box, then trace.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the garment returns the apron. A compound prompt returns a plausible mask that has quietly lost the bough. Background removal on the ring hands back a filled disc, so it is the wrong instrument entirely on an enclosed interior.
trajectory.produces: A raw traced mark with its bough, arch and ring rule all present.

trajectory.action: Perform the vector hygiene the tracer does not, then build the two cuts the set needs: a full mark for the banner and a reduced cut for the six inch plate, each judged at the size it will actually be used.
trajectory.judgement: A trace with no viewBox does not scale and a trace with its ground path intact drops a white box onto every coloured panel. The canvas weave leaves ragged stroke edges that read as texture at banner size and as noise at plate size, so one cut cannot serve both.
trajectory.produces: A placeable transparent full mark and a reduced small size cut, both scalable.

trajectory.action: Knock the staked blank off the gravel so the mockup can stand the sign on the site photograph as a separate placed element.
trajectory.judgement: The stake and the sign's bottom rail sit in the same value range as the wet gravel, which is where any subject detection has the least to work with. The cutout has to be judged against the site frame at full size, not at preview scale.
trajectory.produces: A cut out staked blank with alpha, ready to be placed on the corrected site ground.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for one camera scale outdoor frame for the schedule sheet cover, filter to photography, exclude generative tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the same May morning as the site set, not the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame graded into the site world.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged on whether it reads from a moving car on white coroplast and still feels like a neighbourhood market rather than a municipal notice. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name, and at distance the wrong weight is the whole failure.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the banner root at the fence proportion and a declared scale, the three directional roots, the schedule sheet and the mockup board, each root declaring its own canvas size, every photograph inlined as image data, the mark placed as inline SVG in an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, family and weight declared on every text element, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: Absolute units resolve exactly, so the banner can be authored at true proportion at a scale a sign shop works from, but a photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the artboard, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how much of each sign is instruction and how little is decoration.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole signage set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for every canvas after it.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. A six canvas set checked by looking at the banner is a set with five unchecked canvases.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Convert the sign shop's plate card PDF, export the IDML, and read what the conversion actually exposes as editable frames, with their real bounds and typography, before promising any field to any frame.
trajectory.judgement: What a printed plate looks like and what its PDF converts into are unrelated questions, and the readout the mapping tool hands back is not the document. Promising a mapping before looking is promising something nobody has checked.
trajectory.produces: A real frame inventory with bounds and applied typography, and the reconstructed true story text per frame.

trajectory.action: Compute every offset from the reconstructed story text, prepare the merge template, then confirm by round trip that each field placeholder is genuinely present in the prepared document.
trajectory.judgement: A success message from the prepare step is not evidence a field landed, and offsets computed from the tool's own readout can be short while the validator still reports the mapping valid.
trajectory.produces: A live merge template whose placeholders have been verified rather than assumed.

trajectory.action: Reconcile the roster before anything is printed: resolve the duplicate stall number and the zone spelled two ways, and settle with the committee's own list what the real stall count is.
trajectory.judgement: Forty four plates cut from a file with a duplicate produces a stall nobody can find and a plate nobody claims. The roster is what the committee keeps, not what the printer needs.
trajectory.produces: A reconciled roster with the resolutions stated, and a real stall count.

trajectory.action: Merge the reconciled roster one record per page, render proofs at real print resolution, and read every page rather than the page count.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equal to row count proves the run executed, not that any given plate is right. The only way to know what a long record does inside a frame that already exists is to put it there and look at the page.
trajectory.produces: A press ready plate run with one plate per stall, and print resolution proofs.

trajectory.action: Create the committee board and add the signage set within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the printer note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and the vector mark is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note has to be specific enough that a volunteer can hand it across a counter and get the right thing back.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written printer note.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the parking approach frame can carry a sign at all. The sign has to stand against the fence line, and that frame was shot into the light, so the question is whether there is any information left in the sky behind that fence. A highlight recovery on that region returns success and the readout is that nothing moves: the pixels come back identical because the channel is already fully clipped, and no tool in the connector measures or reports it. Looking at the frame beforehand shows a white sky, which is exactly what a recoverable sky and an unrecoverable one both look like.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no ordering that avoids it, because the answer exists only after the operation has been run and the result compared, and there is no parameter that would have made a clipped channel recoverable. Nothing states it: the client says only that the chair took the photographs one morning in May. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is to change which frame carries the mockup, which changes the composition, or to license and grade an outdoor frame into the same morning, which changes the source.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re plan which frame the staked mockup stands on given that the frame with the fence has a van across the sign position, either recomposing the mockup onto a different site frame or licensing a camera scale outdoor ground and grading it into the same May morning as the rest of the set, then re grading the whole site family so the substituted frame does not read as bought.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A mockup board handed to a committee showing a sign standing against a blank white void where their park's tree line should be, on the one deliverable that exists specifically because half the committee cannot read a plan.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the staked blank can actually be cut off the gravel. The sign's lower edge and its wire stake sit in the same value range as the wet gravel behind them, which is where a knockout has the least to work with, and the tool reports success either way. The returned cutout reads clean and complete at preview scale. Whether the bite has taken the stake, the bottom rail, both or neither on this photograph is a property of this photograph and only appears when the cutout is laid on the site ground at the scale the mockup actually uses.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because subject detection is given no contrast to find at that boundary and reports no confidence for it. Nothing states it: the client supplied the blank purely so the committee could see how big a yard sign is. It is not a propagation re run, because the correct response is a different chain, selecting the gravel field by its own material properties, inverting it and filling, rather than running the one call knockout again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the one call route for that frame, select the gravel as a material by its own visual properties, invert, fill and re cut, then re judge the cutout on the site ground at mockup scale, or recompose the mockup so the compromised boundary sits outside the frame, which changes what the board shows.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A mockup in which the market's new sign appears to float above the gravel with its stake half eaten, presented as the picture the committee approves the whole season's spend from.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What this roster does inside this plate card's existing name frame. The frame is a fixed measure that does not spill: a name longer than the frame does not overflow, wrap or overset, it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, and the merge reports success with a page count that matches the roster exactly. Which vendors this bites, and where in the name the cut lands, is a joint property of the frame's real bounds, the applied face and each individual record, and none of that is visible in any response. The only channel is rendering the run and reading every page.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the behaviour of that frame under that record cannot be known until the record is in the frame, and there is no fitting parameter to set. Nothing states it: the roster is just the roster and the client says the sign shop reprints from this card as is. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a decision about the template and the data, re mapping the name into a frame whose real bounds can hold it, restructuring the field across two lines, or agreeing an abbreviation rule with the committee, each of which changes what is merged rather than merging the same thing again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify every affected record by reading the rendered pages, decide between re mapping the field into a differently bounded frame, restructuring the name field, or agreeing an abbreviation rule, re prepare or re bind accordingly, re merge, re render and read every page again before any plate count is called delivered.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Forty four plates printed on coroplast at a volunteer market's entire signage budget, with a handful of vendors' names cut off mid word at trim, discovered on the Saturday morning they go into the ground.

deliverables.name: Recovered Cedar Commons mark system
deliverables.spec: The market's compound lockup recovered from a photograph of a screen print on coarse canvas as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: bough, arched wordmark and ring rule all present, a real viewBox, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, and the ring's interior genuinely open rather than a filled disc. Delivered as two cuts, a full mark for the banner and a reduced cut that survives at six inches, each judged at the size it is actually used.

deliverables.name: Cedar Commons site photography
deliverables.spec: Four phone frames of the site levelled and brought to one May morning look with one white point and one black point, plus one licensed camera scale outdoor frame graded into the same world so it does not read as bought. Per frame parameter log with one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours, and a plain statement of which frame can carry a sign and which cannot.

deliverables.name: Staked sign cutout and mockup plate
deliverables.spec: The blank coroplast yard sign cut from its gravel ground with alpha intact all the way down the wire stake and along the bottom rail, judged at full size on the site photograph rather than at preview scale, and prepared so the sign face, the site ground and the vector artwork remain three separate placed elements on the mockup canvas rather than one flattened picture.

deliverables.name: Stall plate run, one plate per stall
deliverables.spec: The sign shop's own plate card PDF reverse engineered into a live merge template and bound to the reconciled roster, delivered as one press file with one plate per real stall and a page count equal to the reconciled stall count, every vendor name complete at trim on every page, plus print resolution proofs rendered separately for committee sign off. The roster reconciliation and the bleed limitation are part of the deliverable, not assumptions.

deliverables.name: Signage set as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying the entrance banner at the fence proportion at a declared scale, three directional yard sign roots, the signage schedule sheet and the staked mockup board, each root keeping its own canvas size, with live editable text in one licensed distance legible type system, the mark as real vector shapes and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. Delivered with the self contained source HTML, which is the durable half, because the roster and the layout change every season.

deliverables.name: Printer note and committee board
deliverables.spec: A written note giving substrate, quantity, finished size, declared scale, ink count and safe margin per item, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, every resize any tool reported, the roster reconciliation, what the recovered mark can and cannot do at each size, and what the process could not be given including bleed. Paired with a persistent shareable board the distributed volunteer committee signs off from, with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered mark's SVG carries a viewBox attribute and no full canvas opaque background path at path index zero, and the ring's interior is genuinely open geometry rather than a filled shape.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered SVG: assert a viewBox is present, assert the first path does not span the whole canvas, and assert the ring encloses a hole rather than a fill.

verifiers_auto.text: Two distinct cuts of the mark are delivered and the one used on each canvas is the cut intended for that size.
verifiers_auto.how: Diff the two delivered SVGs for path count and stroke weight, then check which file identifier appears in each canvas of the returned markup.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no tradeoff record captured in the run carries an upscale entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare pixel dimensions of every delivered file against its source per the manifest, and diff the captured tradeoffs objects against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: The staked blank cutout carries genuine alpha along the full length of the stake and the bottom rail rather than terminating early.
verifiers_auto.how: Inspect the alpha channel along the stake column and the bottom rail row for continuous coverage and for full transparency at the frame corners.

verifiers_auto.text: The Express export returned the declared number of roots, each keeping its own declared canvas size, and the banner root's dimensions match the stated fence proportion at the declared scale.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and per slide width and height in the export response and compute the banner root's aspect against the committee's stated fence run.

verifiers_auto.text: No image on any canvas resolved to the importer's placeholder, and the mark arrived as vector path shapes rather than as a single picture, on every canvas that carries it.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the returned per canvas markup for 1x1 placeholder image data and count path shape elements in the mark's region on each canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: The merged plate run has a page count equal to the reconciled stall count, not the raw row count, and no stall number appears twice.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the page count of the merged press file and extract the stall number from every page, asserting uniqueness.

verifiers_auto.text: Every vendor name in the reconciled roster appears in full on its rendered plate, with no record ending at the frame edge.
verifiers_auto.how: Extract the rendered name text from every proof page and compare each against the roster string it came from, character for character.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported markup carries a resolved licensed PostScript face at the numeric weight the family actually defines.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font-family and font-weight attributes on every text node in the returned markup and check them against the families and style inventories the font calls returned.

verifiers_human.text: A volunteer who has worn the apron for nine years recognises the recovered mark as theirs, complete with its bough.
verifiers_human.how: Show the recovered mark beside the apron photograph and ask what is different.

verifiers_human.text: The reduced cut holds at six inches on a plate and the full mark holds read from across a car park, and each is used in the right place.
verifiers_human.how: View each cut at its actual reproduction size, one at plate size in hand and one at banner scale from distance.

verifiers_human.text: Each directional sign delivers one instruction that a driver can read while moving.
verifiers_human.how: View each yard sign at reduced scale from across a room and judge whether the instruction resolves before the type does.

verifiers_human.text: The four site frames read as one morning in one park rather than as four phone photographs, and the licensed frame does not read as bought.
verifiers_human.how: Lay the five frames in a row and judge white point, black point and sky treatment as a set.

verifiers_human.text: The staked sign in the mockup stands in the gravel rather than floating above it, and its stake is whole.
verifiers_human.how: View the mockup board at full size and follow the stake from the sign face to the ground.

verifiers_human.text: The set reads as a cheerful neighbourhood market printed cheaply and well, not as a municipal notice and not as carnival clip art.
verifiers_human.how: Judge palette, ink count, type scale and decoration density against the stated band and audience.

verifiers_human.text: A volunteer could hand the printer note across a sign shop counter and get the right thing back without a phone call.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note as a printer would: substrate, quantity, finished size, scale, ink count and margin per item, plus the limits.

verifiers_human.text: The note tells the committee something they did not already know, including everything that could not be recovered or produced.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and check that the roster reconciliation, the mark's size limits and the bleed limitation are all named.

decision_gates: Which deliverables need an authored fixed canvas document at true physical proportion, which need a genuine record per page run against the sign shop's own template, and which are recovery work.

Selection prompt wording on the apron: naming the garment takes the apron, naming the print's own visual properties takes the ink, a compound prompt loses the bough, and background removal on the ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
How to handle the coarse canvas weave in the trace, given that it reads as texture at banner size and as noise at plate size, and therefore how many cuts of the mark the set actually needs.
Which site frame can carry the staked mockup, given that the one with the fence has a van across the sign position.
Whether to license an outdoor ground and grade it into the site world, or to recompose the mockup onto a frame that already works.
Knockout route on the staked blank: the one call route versus selecting the gravel as a material by its own properties, inverting and filling.
What scale to author the banner at, and how to state that scale so a sign shop outputs the right finished size rather than the canvas size.

The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged on legibility from a moving car on white coroplast, plus the real numeric weight per family, where the wrong weight is the whole failure.
How to resolve a duplicate stall number and a zone spelled two ways, and whether the committee's list or the roster file is authoritative.
What the plate card's exposed frames can actually carry, and whether a long vendor name is solved in the template, in the data, or by an abbreviation rule agreed with the committee.
How few inks and how much white the whole set can be built on, given that everything prints on coroplast and vinyl at a stall fee budget.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the photographs into a frontier image model and it returns charming market signage. IDENTITY: the mark is nine years old, was drawn by a named volunteer's cousin, and is worn on aprons every Saturday by people who will recognise a redraw instantly. It has to be RECOVERED off the apron, not reinvented, and no generated image recovers anything. SPEC: a sign shop prints from a stated finished size at a stated scale on a stated substrate with a stated ink count and a real safe margin, and forty four plates is a per record run whose page count must equal a reconciled stall count with every vendor name complete at trim, which is a hard count and a character comparison, not a picture. EDITABILITY: the roster changes most weeks and the committee is volunteers with no budget to re commission, so the signage set is defined by being a file they can edit. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: is there anything left in that sky, did the cut take the stake, did that vendor's name fit inside a frame that already existed before anyone here was hired.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, the highlight controls, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, remove_background in both forms, and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls. The substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, the compound mark partial selection, the solid disc failure of remove_background on an enclosed ring, the binary mask with no anti aliasing, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are all live findings, and the acceptance bar scores the hygiene no tool performs. Material selection by prompt is verified (a 672,398 pixel wood plank field), which is what makes the gravel route a real alternative to the one call knockout. EXPRESS: exact print canvases via absolute units are verified (210mm by 297mm resolving to exactly 794 by 1123 at 96 dpi), mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, an image left as a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, right anchored auto sized wrappers throw their contents off the artboard, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. The banner is authored at a declared scale rather than at nine thousand pixels, and no print DPI gate is taken off an Express preview, which renders at 1200 px on the long edge. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined site photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are verified headless and synchronous; PDF merge output is one record per page in verified order with page count equal to row count; the lossy textContent readout and the prepare step reporting success while dropping mappings are live findings, which is why offsets are computed from the reconstructed story and placeholders are verified by round trip; resolution is silently ignored on the merge so proofs come only from the render, verified at true 300 DPI; bleed cannot be introduced from a PDF sourced template and pdfPreset is unusable, so neither is gated and both are named in the note. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including the case sensitivity trap and the non standard numeric weights. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returns genuine camera scale, boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no upscaling, no object removal (the van is handled by choosing a different frame), no photo compositing tool (the mockup is separate placed elements on an authored canvas), no OCR, no text to image, no fill_text, no animate_design, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.
